summary: The note describes how local schools are adopting collaborative interdisciplinary projects that combine subjects such as science, arts, history, technology, and math. It gives examples from several schools, covers challenges like scheduling and assessment alignment, and discusses how impact is measured through engagement and social growth as well as test scores. It concludes that these projects better prepare students for modern workplaces and reflect a shift toward holistic education.
one_line: Local schools are adopting interdisciplinary projects across subjects, with examples, challenges, and benefits for student engagement, teamwork, and future readiness.
key_facts: Jefferson High School began a community waste management project on September 10, 2023, involving arts, sciences, and humanities students.
Maria Gonzalez (Environmental Science) and Paul Singh (Visual Arts) guided the Jefferson High School waste management project.
On October 5, 2023, Eastwood Elementary showcased its 'History Meets Technology' exhibition, where students reenacted historical events using robotic figures they programmed themselves.
Richard Lee (history teacher) and Jane Murphy (computer science instructor) spearheaded the Eastwood Elementary exhibition.
Westdale Middle School started a project on November 2, 2023 combining mathematics and physical education to study the geometry of sports movements.
Craig Turner, math coach at Westdale Middle School, described logistical challenges such as coordinating time slots and resources between departments.
Common hurdles for interdisciplinary projects include aligning teaching schedules, managing different assessment standards, and ensuring all subjects get equal importance.
At Lincoln Academy, an environmental policy project launched in September merged civics with science, and Principal Emily Harris noted a significant increase in student engagement.
Riverview International School's 'Global Cultures Festival', led by Damien Brooks and Alicia Fernandez, has run since mid-September and evaluates academic, social, and personal growth.
Laura Philips of Evergreen High School, who is involved in a biology and digital design project, said technology enabled seamless collaboration among students who might otherwise never cross paths.
Students from Claymore High in the Baytown School District took part in an interdisciplinary competition on December 15, 2023, developing a sustainable business model for a local organic farm.
The note says implementation of these projects across local schools is still in the nascent stages.
